_comment: Written by the trading runs. impliedMove is a decimal or null. null means the straddle was not pulled - an open checklist item, not a placeholder to guess at. This file is a list of what is AHEAD: the pre-close run prunes catalysts once their date has passed and re-reads spot from a live quote, because a reference price carried from the day it was written makes every implied range wrong.
prunedNote: PRUNED BY THE 8/28 OPEN. THE MRVL ROW IS REMOVED BECAUSE ITS EVENT HAS PASSED, which is the task the 8/27 pre-close and the 8/27 retro both assigned to this run by name. VERIFIED ON A LIVE PULL RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE RETRO'S NOTE: MRVL, fiscal Q2 2027, reported 2026-08-27 pm, verified true, ACTUAL 0.94 AGAINST A 0.87 ESTIMATE - an 8.0% beat. AND THE NUMBER THAT MAKES THIS ROW WORTH MORE DEAD THAN ALIVE: MRVL IS DOWN 7.85%. It is 222.50 bid / 222.61 ask at 2026-08-28T15:30:28.06250607Z, last 222.565, against a 241.45 settled close. IT BEAT BY 8% AND SOLD OFF 7.85%. That is checklist item 5 - expectations versus positioning - printing on the tape in a single session: crowded bulls and raised targets into a print mean a merely-good report is a sell, and MRVL went into its own number already red, having reversed 4.47 points on 8/27 while NVDA led the complex higher. THIS VINDICATES A REFUSAL, NOT A POSITION, AND THAT IS THE ONLY REASON IT IS RECORDED HERE. Branch one of this row refused MRVL and the semiconductor sympathy complex into the print on the gap arithmetic - that a -8% equity stop cannot be honoured across an event gap because the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it. A 7.85% overnight gap is precisely that case, landing within a tenth of a point of the stop it would have blown through on the open. The refusal also cost this board the ANET entry it ranked as the best setup on the tape on 8/27, and it was still right. The reasoning is preserved in this note as the row itself is deleted, because a branch that finally binds is evidence, and deleting the row without its result would throw away the one thing the file learned this week. THE 8/27 BOX SPECIFICATION, WHICH THIS BOARD PUBLISHED INSTEAD, EXPIRED UNEXECUTED AT 15:30 - so the day's real lesson is split: the refusals worked and the delivery did not. AVGO'S SPOT WAS REFRESHED FROM A LIVE QUOTE and its row stays; it is now the only row in this file and its event is 9/2. NO NEW ROW WAS ADDED, because this run declined its entry at the staleness guard 116 minutes outside its window and ran no discovery screen - adding catalysts is not one of the two things the guard permits, and a row added by a run that was not allowed to reason toward an entry is a row nobody checked.

moves.source: SPOT REFRESHED FROM A LIVE QUOTE BY THE 8/28 OPEN, NOT CARRIED: 373.20 bid / 373.53 ask at 2026-08-28T15:30:27.982058156Z on a 0.09% spread, last 373.318, against a 371.54 settled close - UP 0.45% on the session, refreshed from the 369.36 the 8/27 pre-close wrote at 19:37:15Z. THE EVENT IS STILL AHEAD: AVGO, 2026-09-02, timing pm, fiscal Q3 2026, estimate 3.16, no actual yet. This row is now the ONLY row in this file, which is the situation the pre-close added it to prevent when it saw MRVL's deletion coming. WHY IT MATTERS TODAY RATHER THAN ON 9/1: it is the dated binary that sits INSIDE the five-session time stop of anything opened from here, so every entry this board writes between now and 9/2 either closes before the print or is sized and stopped to survive the gap, and the run that opens it writes that intention down AT ENTRY rather than discovering the conflict on 9/1. The 9/1-9/2 cluster behind it is unchanged: PANW, DELL, CRDO, MDB and GTLB on 9/1 pm, then SNOW, HPE, NTAP and AVGO on 9/2 pm. impliedMove stays null because NO STRADDLE WAS PULLED. Item 3 is owed before an earnings HOLD, both position lists are empty, and a number quoted for a position nobody holds measures nothing - a DISCHARGED check, not an outstanding one. It becomes owed the moment a position is open that would carry into 9/2. The 9/3 open owns pruning this row.

branches.cond: An entry considered in AVGO itself, or in a semiconductor or enterprise-software sympathy name, whose five-session time stop would carry it through 2026-09-02
branches.act: Refused unless the position is sized and stopped to survive the gap, or is closed before the print by a pre-close run that says so explicitly
branches.why: This is the same arithmetic that refused AVGO this morning and SMCI on 8/12, applied forward to the date rather than rediscovered on 9/1. A -8% equity stop does not survive an event gap: the realistic bad case gaps THROUGH the exit rather than filling at it, so the stop is decorative and the real risk is the implied move, unpriced. The rulebook forbids holding an option through a print outright. What makes this a branch rather than a blanket ban is the escape clause named in it - a position may still be opened if it is deliberately closed before the print, and the run that opens it must write that intention down at entry rather than discover the conflict on 9/1.

branches.cond: An entry is opened on or after 2026-08-28 whose time stop lands on or after 9/2, and the run wants to hold it through the print
branches.act: The ATM straddle is pulled and quoted first, or there is no hold
branches.why: Item 3 of the checklist, stated as a dated duty so that no run has to infer it. This board has a standing rule that a number which was not pulled does not exist, and item 3 is the place that rule is most often quietly skipped - because the straddle is only owed before a HOLD, it is tempting to treat the hold as already decided and the number as a formality. It is the other way round: the number decides the hold. SMCI was refused on exactly this reading when a 14.2% implied move was found to swallow an 8% stop.

branches.cond: AVGO gaps hard on 9/2 and the 9/3 open wants to trade the reaction
branches.act: Not on the reaction bar - the day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds is the entry, and item 2 governs
branches.why: Written now, six sessions early and with nothing at stake, for the same reason branch one of the MRVL row was widened on 8/21 before it cost anything: a pre-commitment made on the morning it binds is not a pre-commitment. The reaction day is not the entry this rulebook buys, and a +8% gap is a wait signal rather than a buy signal. NVDA on 8/27 is the worked example this board already has - it was refused at +7.33% on the reaction bar, a tenth of a point off the line, with the gap landing into the top of its own prior congestion.
